title: This 3.1-Mile Table Is Made From Recycled Materials!
summary:
Picture a table so long you can't see the end of it. On September 12, 2026, about 20,000 people gathered in Bucharest, Romania, for a community meal. Their table set a new Guinness World Record for the longest table made from recycled materials.

The table was called the "Uniting Table." It stretched 3.1 miles (4.99 km).

But the record was only part of the plan. The event, organized by a nonprofit called Bloom The World, was also a fundraiser. It raised more than $110,000 for Romania's first psychiatric hospital for children. Right now, children in Bucharest who need mental health care are treated in an outdated building. It has large, crowded wards that lack basic privacy. The new hospital is set to open in 2027. It will care for children with conditions such as depression, autism and ADHD.

This was the second time Bloom set this record. In 2025, the group brought 10,000 people together around a 1.7-mile (2.7 km) table made from recycled materials in Alba Iulia, Romania.

So what happens to the table when dinner is over? Bloom plans to recycle its materials again. This time, they will be used to make furniture for children.
why_it_matters: It shows how a fun record can also help children who need care, and how old materials can be used again.
